content: Radiofrequency saphenous vein ablation may be indicated when ALL of the following are present:

children.content: Incompetence of saphenous vein documented by duplex ultrasound or other imaging test with valve closure time of greater than 500 msec
children.question: Is there documentation of incompetence of the saphenous vein with a valve closure time greater than 500 msec in the patient's medical record?

children.content: Saphenous venous insufficiency symptoms causing functional impairment, including 1 or more of the following:
Bleeding or ruptured superficial varicose veins
children.question: Is there documentation of bleeding or ruptured superficial varicose veins in the patient's medical record, along with saphenous venous insufficiency symptoms causing functional impairment?
Is there documentation of leg edema in the patient's medical record?
Does the patient experience leg fatigue due to saphenous venous insufficiency symptoms causing functional impairment?
Is there documentation of leg pain in the patient's medical record related to saphenous venous insufficiency symptoms causing functional impairment?
Is there documentation of persistent or recurrent superficial thrombophlebitis in the patient's medical record?

children.content: Persistent or recurrent venous stasis ulcer
children.question: Is there documentation of a persistent or recurrent venous stasis ulcer in the patient's medical record?
Does the patient exhibit skin changes such as lipodermatosclerosis or hemosiderosis in the context of saphenous venous insufficiency symptoms causing functional impairment?

children.content: No clinically significant lower extremity arterial disease
children.question: Is there documentation in the medical record indicating that the patient does not have clinically significant lower extremity arterial disease?

children.content: No deep venous thrombosis on duplex ultrasound or other imaging test
children.question: Is there documentation in the medical record showing no deep venous thrombosis on duplex ultrasound or other imaging test?
